title: Wewelsburg Castle seances of Himmler's SS knights

tellings.quote: Right. Which I went to and I did a a TV thing like 10, 15 years ago, 20 years ago for that on that. And that's a a beautiful castle, but was in disrepair when Himmler took it over. He refurbished it with concentration camp labor and he built basically uh a roundt for his 12 knights to sit around and have seances, right?
He turned Wewelsburg Castle into a ritual center, complete with a black sun chamber beneath it, and a round table for his SS knights.
tellings.difference: Adds a black sun chamber beneath the castle and doesn't mention seances or concentration camp labor.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell of Himmler turning Wewelsburg Castle into a ritual center with a round table for his SS knights.

plain: In the 1930s Heinrich Himmler, head of the SS, the Nazi elite guard, is said to have turned Wewelsburg Castle in Germany into a ritual center for his men. The author Peter Levenda, who writes about the Nazis and the occult, says he visited the castle and filmed a TV program there years ago. He says it was in disrepair when Himmler took it over, that it was rebuilt with concentration camp labor, and that Himmler built a round table for "his 12 knights to sit around and have seances." Jesse Michels tells it in another episode, saying Himmler made the castle a ritual center "complete with a black sun chamber beneath it," a room under the castle, along with the round table for his SS knights. Michels does not mention seances or the camp labor. The tellers bring it up to show how deeply occult belief ran at the top of the Nazi state.
